about: Two-layer (guard + undercoat) parameters per roster species. Derived from A19 SPECIES_FUR.md layer extensions (density ratios, sourced lengths) and A11 FUR_COLOUR.md profiles (layer colours). [S] = sourced in A19/A11, [E] = A16 estimate ordered to agree with sourced facts. Ratios are per torso.back unless noted; full per-region ratios live in A19.

global_rules.note: A19 layer.undercoat is a coverage/density dial (undercoat density relative to guard density in the zone), NOT a strand-count ratio. Because undercoat strands are ~half the radius, a groom needs a strand-count ratio well above the coverage ratio to deliver it.

badger.guard_colour_pattern: banded (white base, black subterminal band — the banding IS the grey)
badger.layer_notes: The inverted badger: guard hair is the show layer and the silhouette; the undercoat barely exists and the belly is sparse by design (skin visible). Two-layer geometry spend is unjustified — texture-floor undercoat (root colour in the pelt) only.
badger.undercoat_length_basis: [E] ratio-derived; undercoat described as sparse and soft [S]

bear.layer_notes: Undercoat is a loft engine: long guards (to 0.12 m at withers) over woolly underfur. Sen's ruff takes moon-bear values; chest crescent is a colour zone only, layer structure unchanged.

seasonal.note: heavy late-spring moult; summer coat thinner/shabbier [S]

undercoat_colour.note: grizzle lives in the GUARD tipping (pale tips), not the undercoat

bear.undercoat_length_basis: [E] ratio-derived; underfur described as dense and woolly [S]

clydesdale.layer_notes: Not the carnivore plan: a seasonal underhair appears under the winter body coat only. The identity systems (mane, tail, feather, forelock) are single-layer continuous-growth hair at EVERY season — layer split applies to the body regions and nowhere else.
clydesdale.undercoat_length_basis: [S] winter underhair 2.2-2.9 cm in free-ranging horses; winter outer mean 4.7 cm temperate [S]

fennec.layer_notes: Desert inversion of the fox plan: the double coat is insulation in both directions. ears.inner is a single layer of long fine hair (exception zone); feet carry undercoat over the pads (unique on roster).

seasonal.note: no annual cycle — daily temperature swing; dense undercoat insulates against cold desert nights [S]

lion.layer_notes: The control case: NO undercoat layer anywhere. All fur information is guard-class hair (body coat + mane system). Any two-layer spend on a lion is waste — this is the species that proves the layer split must be data-driven, not universal.

red_fox.layer_notes: Follicles group as triads: 1 guard + 2 intermediate + a bundle of awn underfur [S]. The intermediate hairs are a genuine third population (between guard and underfur in length/stiffness) — the only roster species where a 2-layer model is a simplification of a 3-layer reality.

undercoat_colour.note: grey underfur [S]; visible where the coat parts — record root colour should be the grey, tip the rufous (A19)

red_fox.undercoat_length_basis: [S] underfur ~35 mm measured; guard dorsal mean ~60 mm [S]

saint_bernard.layer_notes: Bred double coat: resilient close-lying outer over a short dense soft undercoat. One profile, variety switch (smooth|rough) changes lengths only, never the layer plan.

seasonal.note: biannual coat blow instead of a summer length table [S]

undercoat_colour.note: white ground with red/brown patches is markings; fur within a patch is solid root~tip (A19)

saint_bernard.undercoat_length_basis: [E]; undercoat described as 'short, very dense, and soft' (UKC standard) [S]

wolf.layer_notes: Reference double coat. Undercoat hides skin completely at prime winter density (A19 normalisation anchor 1.0).

seasonal.note: the undercoat is the seasonal variable; summer wolf reads leggy/narrow because this layer is gone [S]

wolf.undercoat_length_basis: [E] ratio-derived (fox is the measured anchor at 0.58)
